Romance-scam losses reported to the FBI reached $672 million in 2024.

entries.answer: Deepfake fraud is now routine: identity-verification firm Entrust detected a deepfake attempt every five minutes in 2024. Scammers use AI-generated faces and video in romance and investment scams as well as attacks on businesses. Because people can't reliably spot deepfakes by eye, check suspicious images with a detector and verify identities on a live video call.

Sextortion is rising fast and mostly targets teenage boys. Thorn's analysis of NCMEC CyberTipline data found an average of 812 sextortion reports per week, and 90% of victims in those reports were male, aged 14 to 17. AI-generated fake nudes mean scammers no longer need a real image to threaten someone.
